tool_args.content:
% Section 7 — Discussion and Conclusion

We validated OntoCoDec across 2 RE datasets, 3 model families, and event extraction (\S\ref{sec:wikievents}).
The central finding is non-additive layer interaction: grammar alone achieves 3\% DR reduction on SciERC, semantic alone 24\%, but their composition yields 94\% at 8B (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results})---grammar-enforced vocabulary membership creates the clean input the semantic layer requires.

\paragraph{Scale-dependent layer interaction.}
This dependency weakens at scale: at 70B, the semantic layer independently achieves 84\% DR reduction (\S\ref{sec:70b-results}).
We offer a speculative hypothesis: larger models exhibit improved vocabulary calibration, assigning higher probability to ontology-valid tokens and reducing the semantic layer's dependence on grammar-enforced vocabulary membership (Appendix~\ref{app:causal-tracing}); confirming this causal mechanism requires cross-family verification beyond our current scope.
Fallback frequency varies dramatically across architectures (0 vs.\ 5{,}882 under LoRA+S1) without affecting enforcement (both DR\,$\leq$\,0.21\%), confirming grammar is necessary but increasingly insufficient as models improve.
Constraint enforcement is preserved under INT4 quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).

\paragraph{DR$\leftrightarrow$CF trade-off.}
Greedy S1 reduces DR to $\leq$\,0.21\% but introduces CF (zero-shot $+$9.82\,pp, fine-tuned $+$1.18\,pp)---an architectural consequence of per-triple independent enforcement.
Among 248 zero-shot CF violations, 58.1\% involve hallucinated entities (absent from gold) and only 7.3\% are true cascade errors (\S\ref{sec:scierc-results}); fine-tuned CF drops to $\leq$1.4\%.
Beam $k{=}2$ reduces CF to 0.11\% at 1.18$\times$ latency (Pareto-optimal; recommended for zero-shot deployment); $k{=}4$ eliminates all violations at 8B at 1.39$\times$ (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).

\paragraph{Complementarity and deployment.}
GoLLIE and KnowCoder internalize schema knowledge via training but lack runtime guarantees; LoRA + S1 shows the two are complementary (DR 1--2\%\,$\to$\,$\leq$0.21\%).
S2 (two-pass) degrades at 70B ($-$8\,pp R-F1), consistent with CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane}; we recommend S1 as default.
The root cause---per-triple enforcement cannot coordinate cross-triple type assignments (Level~3; \S\ref{sec:decidability})---requires global entity-level consensus beyond online masking; beam search and TCR approximate this, with full integration as future work.

\paragraph{70B-class validation (single-family).}
\label{sec:70b-results}
The following results constitute a preliminary single-family scale exploration on Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (Activation-aware Weight Quantization (AWQ) INT4); cross-family verification (e.g., Qwen-72B) remains future work.
All 70B experiments use Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct under AWQ INT4 quantization; an 8B ablation confirms constraint enforcement is unaffected by quantization (Appendix~\ref{app:quantization}).
Zero-shot S1 eliminates DR on both datasets (SciERC 6.41\%\,$\to$\,0\%, DocRED 14.98\%\,$\to$\,0\%; R-F1 11--13).
% exp_ids: r16_70b_scierc_zs_ablation (grammar_only, semantic_only, full_s1)
A four-way ablation reveals scale-dependent layer interaction: semantic-only achieves 84\% DR reduction vs.\ 8B's 24\% (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}), though grammar remains necessary for RV elimination and CF control (semantic-only CF${=}$76).
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_scierc_s1_constrained, eval_70b_lora_docred_200_s1_constrained
LoRA confirms composability: DR\,$\to$\,0\% on both datasets (R-F1 44.53, 43.95; $|\Delta| \leq 0.20$\,pp; CF 0.18--1.33\%); cross-family generalization at 70B scale remains to be verified.
% exp_ids: eval_70b_lora_docred_200_beam4_s1
Beam ($k{=}4$) reduces DocRED parse failures (12.5\%\,$\to$\,0.5\%, R-F1 $+$4.19\,pp); SciERC controlled comparison isolates pure beam gain at $+$0.28\,pp (Appendices~\ref{app:70b-ablation},~\ref{app:70b-docred-zs},~\ref{app:70b-docred}).

% exp_ids: trie_qwen_ft_scierc, trie_qwen_zs_scierc, trie_llama_ft_scierc, trie_llama_zs_scierc
\paragraph{Comparison with grammar-constrained approaches.}
\label{sec:constrained-baselines}
Our grammar-only ablation (Table~\ref{tab:scierc-ablation}, row~2) implements the same constraints as GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd} and BoostCD~\cite{boostcd2025}; vLLM \texttt{guided\_json}~\cite{kwon2023vllm} confirms equivalence on Qwen3-8B (DR${=}$15.26\%; other models use the same backend; Appendix~\ref{app:gcd-comparison}).
The ${\sim}$15\% residual DR is the gap our semantic layer addresses (94\% total reduction); trie-only constraints without JSON enforcement yield 9--51\% parse failure (Appendix~\ref{app:trie-baseline}).

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Cross-field violation analysis.}
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (ZS: CF=248, 167 docs), w5_lora_scierc_full_s1_eval (FT: CF=21, 20 docs)
Under zero-shot greedy S1, CF is the sole residual violation type (DR, RV, ET all eliminated): 248 cross-field violations arise across 167 documents, of which 63.3\% involve \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X type ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}), concentrated in \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{OtherScientificTerm} (34.7\%) and \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\textsc{Material} (12.3\%).
A source breakdown (Appendix~\ref{app:cascade-analysis}) shows 58.1\% originate from hallucinated entities (a model capacity issue), while true cascade errors---where first-seen registration locks an incorrect type---account for only 7.3\%; correct locks are 2.5$\times$ more frequent, confirming first-seen registration as a net-positive mechanism.
Fine-tuning reduces CF to 21 cross-field violation instances across 20 documents (1.18\%), with cascade errors completely eliminated (0/21).
Beam search ($k{=}4$) eliminates all remaining CF at 1.39$\times$ latency (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Cross-field violation analysis.}
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (ZS: CF=248, 167 docs), w5_lora_scierc_full_s1_eval (FT: CF=21, 20 docs)
Under zero-shot greedy S1, CF is the sole residual violation type (DR, RV, ET all eliminated): 248 violations across 167 documents, 63.3\% involving \textsc{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$X type ambiguity (Appendix~\ref{app:cf-distribution}).
A source breakdown shows 58.1\% originate from hallucinated entities, while true cascade errors account for only 7.3\% (Appendix~\ref{app:cascade-analysis}); fine-tuning reduces CF to 1.18\% with cascade errors eliminated; beam $k{=}4$ eliminates all remaining CF (\S\ref{sec:beam-results}).
